summary.headline: Kaveri Seed Q1 FY27 revenue fell to Rs 815 crore from Rs 945 crore (about -14%) on a weak El Nino monsoon, with EBITDA margin held near 35%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 815 crore against Rs 945 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA at Rs 285 crore (vs Rs 332 crore) and net profit at Rs 271.3 crore (vs Rs 316 crore) as stated on the call. Management attributed the decline to a delayed, deficient monsoon that shortened the sowing window, cutting maize sales in Karnataka and weakening demand in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Gujarat. Cotton was flat YoY at Rs 213.43 crore while non-cotton was Rs 601.57 crore, and new products gained share in cotton and maize. Management said the quarter's margin was helped by lower production cost (down 4-5%) and that inventory is up about Rs 200 crore YoY, prompting lower production next year.

financial_highlights.change: same as last year, management said slightly above
about Rs 265-270 crore as of 30 June

segments.name: Cotton
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 213.43 crore, flat YoY. New cotton products were 37% of cotton sales vs 22% last year; North India (Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan) roughly doubled from a small base, while Gujarat and Maharashtra were hit by low rain and illegal Bt seed.

segments.name: Maize
segments.commentary: Sales fell sharply (about 40% decline per analyst question, not disputed by management); Karnataka sowing was about one-fifth done by mid-June. New single-cross hybrids are over 20% of maize sales.

segments.name: Hybrid rice
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 247.07 crore, the largest non-cotton segment. Two new hybrids KRH7344 and KRH7227 launched this season contributed 62% of new-product sales in rice.

segments.name: Selection rice
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 159.07 crore, marginal YoY growth despite poor rain in rice sowing areas.

segments.name: Bajra
segments.commentary: New hybrids are 65% of Bajra volumes, up from 61%.

segments.name: Vegetables
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 15.08 crore; management called it a small segment with some spillover possible in Q2 if rain improves.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the rest of FY27 quarters to be higher than the prior year's comparable quarters, with Karnataka recovery and Rabi maize supporting H2; the Q1 revenue gap is expected to narrow but no full recovery was committed.
Management said Q2 margins would be lower than Q1 margins, and that the YoY revenue gap would narrow, not turn positive, within FY27.
Karnataka Kharif recovery: about 1,500 tonnes sold this year vs about 2,600 tonnes last year, a gap of 1,100-1,200 tonnes worth about Rs 40-60 crore (figures given inconsistently on the call).
Export target of Rs 100 crore in vegetables and other crops within about 3 years; export margin expected at 25-30%, in line with current levels.
Management reiterated a long-term growth target of 15-18% (earlier referenced as 18-20%) over the next 2-3 years, with growth expected to return to last year's level.
Cash expected to rise only by about Rs 20-30 crore by Q2 to close to Rs 300 crore; any buyback is subject to a Board decision, with no amount decided.
capex_capacity: Inventory is up about Rs 200 crore YoY because production was taken up on expectations of a good El Nino-era season; management said production will be reduced next year.
Cost of production is down 4-5% YoY while dealer-level realisations are down 2-3%; management said FY28 production will be minimal and cost per unit should stay at last year's level.
Product pipeline described as among the best in 10 years, with Madhya Pradesh hybrids newer and not yet at scale.
demand_pricing: Monsoon deficit to June 15 shortened the Kharif sowing window and farmers bought fewer premium products; Karnataka tanks now filling after July rains, which management expects to support maize in Q2-Q3.
Maize price rose to about Rs 27-28 from Rs 16-17 at the start of the season, which management expects to support Rabi demand.
Cotton MRP is government-capped; management said Kaveri realises higher prices than many peers in the top three cotton segments.
Competition: illegal Bt cotton and smaller players have grown; management said no new hybrids from peers have taken share in the last 3-4 years, and that Kaveri has lost cotton share over 7-8 years.
Management said subsidiaries (sales of about 10-12 lakh cotton packets this year) operate as separate competitors, and that their revenue is booked independently.

qa_highlights.question: Why has profit not crossed the ~Rs 300 crore peak of 2014-15 despite non-cotton growth, and what can be achieved in 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cotton was about 90% of mix in 2014-15 at high margins versus about 20% now, with cotton margins shrunk; FY27 was a one-off weather year and should not be a benchmark.

qa_highlights.question: Is Kaveri losing focus on cotton given illegal seed, price caps and no new cotton hybrids; what about the inventory build of about Rs 1,200 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management admitted cotton share was lost over 7-8 years, said new hybrids were developed in the last 3-4 years, and said inventory is about Rs 200 crore higher YoY due to over-anticipated El Nino season; production will be reduced next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins not fall with lower sales, and is any crop's margin lower than last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA margin slightly expanded; gross margin up 2-3%, with higher employee and other costs as people were deployed ahead of an expected good season.

qa_highlights.question: Why are subsidiaries selling seeds alongside Kaveri, and what is the new-product definition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said subsidiaries are independent competitors that take discarded me-too hybrids; about 10-12 lakh cotton packets sold through subsidiaries this year. New products are those launched within the last 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did maize fall about 40% when peers grew, and what about Karnataka recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed weak rain in Karnataka, Andhra and Telangana (25-30% of last year's Kharif sales came from Karnataka) and no Madhya Pradesh or Maharashtra presence; Karnataka sales were about 1,500 tonnes vs 2,600 tonnes, a gap of 1,100-1,200 tonnes worth about Rs 40-60 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue outlook and cash/buyback position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 quarters should be above last year's, Q2 margins lower than Q1, and the YoY gap should narrow but not turn positive. Cash of Rs 265-270 crore as of 30 June may rise only Rs 20-30 crore to about Rs 300 crore by Q2; buyback is a Board decision with no amount decided.

risks_watch: Karnataka maize recovery (about Rs 40-60 crore gap) depends on Kharif rain and tank filling; management has not committed to full recovery.
Inventory build of about Rs 200 crore YoY; production cuts planned for next year and inventory holding cost/realisation pressure (dealer realisations down 2-3%).
Cotton margin compression (management cited cotton EBITDA near 15% vs 35% earlier) and continued illegal Bt cotton in Gujarat and Maharashtra.
Weak Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra presence where peers gained maize share; new MP hybrids not yet at scale.
Target slippage: 15-18% long-term growth target (earlier 18-20%) and expectation of return to prior-year growth in 2-3 years; export target of Rs 100 crore in about 3 years.
Subsidiary structure competing with Kaveri; Q2 margin guidance lower than Q1 and cash expected to be flat near Rs 300 crore.

summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the long-term pipeline and new cotton and rice hybrids but cautious on near-term numbers, calling FY27 a one-off weather year and declining to commit to full revenue recovery. Answers on subsidiaries, cotton share loss and inconsistent figures (Karnataka gap, cost reduction, rice share) were often vague or corrected mid-answer.

growth.why: Q1 revenue fell about 14% YoY to Rs 815 crore on a delayed, deficient monsoon; management expects the YoY gap to narrow but not turn positive in FY27 and reiterated a 15-18% long-term growth target, with no specific capacity or order numbers behind the recovery.
